questions.q: Which plural *you* is used for friends in Spain but not in Latin America?
questions.explain: Spain uses *vosotros* as the informal plural; Latin America uses *ustedes* for everyone.

questions.q: In central Spain, *gracias* is pronounced with…
questions.explain: *Distinción*: *c* before *e/i* and *z* sound like *th* in most of Spain.

questions.q: Hoy *___* paella. (Spain, earlier today)
questions.explain: Spain uses the present perfect for events earlier today.

questions.q: In Argentina, *Where are you from?* is usually…
questions.explain: With *vos*, *ser* becomes *sos*.

questions.q: The *vos* form of *tener* is…
questions.explain: *Vos* forms are stressed on the ending and have no stem change: *tenés*.

questions.q: In Buenos Aires, *me llamo* sounds like…
questions.explain: Rioplatense Spanish pronounces *ll* and *y* as /ʃ/ or /ʒ/ (*sheísmo*).

questions.q: *Laburo* in Argentina means…
questions.explain: *Laburo* comes from Italian *lavoro*, work.

questions.q: In Mexico, *¿Mande?* is used to…
options: ask someone to repeat or answer a call politely
questions.explain: *¿Mande?* is the polite Mexican way to say *Pardon?* or *Yes?*

questions.q: A Mexican friend says *¡Qué padre!* They mean…
questions.explain: *Padre* (and *chido*) mean *cool, great* in Mexico.

questions.q: In Mexico, *camión* usually means…
questions.explain: In Mexico a *camión* is also a city bus.

questions.q: In the Caribbean, *¿cómo estás?* often sounds like…
questions.explain: Final *s* is aspirated or dropped in Caribbean Spanish.

questions.q: Which question order is typical of Caribbean Spanish?
questions.explain: Caribbean speakers often put the subject before the verb in questions.

questions.q: A *guagua* in Cuba or Puerto Rico is…
questions.explain: *Guagua* means bus in the Caribbean and the Canary Islands (in Chile it means baby).

questions.q: In Puerto Rico, *Puerto Rico* is often pronounced…
questions.explain: Syllable-final *r* often becomes *l* in Puerto Rican Spanish.

questions.q: In the Dominican Republic, *vaina* means…
questions.explain: *Vaina* is an all-purpose word for *thing* in the Dominican Republic (and Colombia, Panama, Venezuela).

questions.q: In Colombia, *un tinto* is…
questions.explain: In Colombia *tinto* is black coffee; in Spain it's red wine.

questions.q: Many Colombians use *___* even with family and close friends.
questions.explain: In Bogotá and the Andes, *usted* expresses respect and affection, even at home.

questions.q: *Parce* in Colombia means…
questions.explain: *Parce / parcero* means friend.

questions.q: *¿Me regala un café?* in a Colombian shop means…
options: Will you give me a gift?
questions.explain: *Regalar* is a polite way to ask for something you will pay for.

questions.q: *¿Qué xopá?* is Panamanian for…
questions.explain: It is *¿Qué pasó?* with the syllables reversed.

questions.q: Many Panamanian slang words, like *buay* and *guial*, come from…
questions.explain: Close contact with the USA around the canal brought many English loanwords.

questions.q: In Spain, *Vale* means…
questions.explain: *Vale* is the everyday Spanish way to say OK.

questions.q: *Ordenador* (Spain) is *___* in most of Latin America.
questions.explain: Latin America uses *computadora* (or *computador*).

questions.q: Which verb is neutral in Spain but vulgar in much of Latin America?
questions.explain: Use *tomar* or *agarrar* in Latin America instead of *coger*.

questions.q: The *vos* command of *venir* (Argentina) is…
questions.explain: *Vos* commands drop the final *r* and stress the ending: *vení, hablá, comé*.
